scope: A4 research record: which data sources can fill the empty large-scale cells (and the three remaining small-scale gaps). Research only; nothing downloaded yet. Sizes are estimates from atom counts where the server gives no length.

evidence_routes.measured_structure: Experimental atomic coordinates (PDB/COD); answers computed from coordinates.
evidence_routes.derived_representation: Measured coordinates reduced deterministically (e.g. symmetry expansion, chain centroids) because the full atom list is too large to give to a model; the reduction is disclosed.
evidence_routes.paper_parameter_model: Structure built from parameters reported in a paper (lattice constant, particle size, twist angle); geometry is exact for the stated model but not an observed atom list.
evidence_routes.none_found: No suitable public structure found yet.

sources.what: GroEL–GroES–(ADP)7 chaperonin, 14+7 subunits, X-ray 3.0 Å, 58,870 atoms
Nucleosome core particle NCP147, X-ray 1.94 Å, 16,755 atoms
Satellite tobacco mosaic virus capsid (T=1, 60 copies from BIOMT), about 17 nm

families: global_extent / equal_weight_rg at assembly scale
guinier_intensity (existing) at small q
fret_efficiency (existing) across a ring or particle
new: assembly_symmetry (subunit count and ring / icosahedral spacing from BIOMT)
cells.risks: Capsid questions need symmetry expansion; must use the deposited BIOMT operators, not guessed symmetry.

sources.what: HSV-1 capsid with tegument complexes, cryo-EM 4.2 Å, 219,702 atoms per asymmetric unit; icosahedral T=16, about 125 nm, 960 copies of major capsid protein

families: capsid extent from expanded chain centroids
new: capsomer counting / T-number from the expanded assembly
nearest-neighbour capsomer spacing (coordination_shell analogue on centroids)
cells.risks: Full expansion is ~13 M atoms: the model receives per-chain centroids (about 3,000 points), a disclosed reduction.

sources.what: DNA origami 16-helix bundle, cryo-EM 10 Å pseudo-atomic model, 54,985 atoms, 37 chains (Kube et al., Nat. Commun. 2020)

families: global extent / bundle length
new: helix-packing spacing (inter-axis distance of the square/honeycomb lattice)
fret_efficiency (DNA-origami FRET rulers are a real use case)
cells.risks: 10 Å map: pseudo-atomic coordinates; questions must stay at helix / bundle scale, not base-pair detail.

sources.what: oxDNA coarse-grained DNA/RNA nanostructure designs, some ≥100 nm
sources.license: per structure; many entries list N/A
sources.download: only entries with an explicit open license

families: same as 10-100 on coarse-grained nucleotides, if a licensed ≥100 nm structure exists
cells.risks: No atomistic public structure found; coarse models are designs or simulations, not measurements. Needs a decision from the professor.

sources.what: Particle-centre lattices with lattice constants of tens of nm (e.g. Shevchenko et al., Nature 2006)
sources.license: parameters are facts; paper text not redistributed

sources.what: Measured 3D coordinates of an 8.4 nm FePt nanoparticle (23,196 atoms) in the Materials Data Bank
sources.download: not attempted (site unreachable during research); 8.4 nm is the 1-10 cell

families: coordination_shell on particle centres
first-order superlattice diffraction (inference)
cells.risks: Measured atomistic structures at 10-100 nm are rare; the superlattice route is a model from reported parameters and must say so.

sources.what: FCC packings of ~240-300 nm silica spheres; (111) Bragg reflection in the visible (e.g. Phys. Rev. B 72, 205115 (2005))
sources.license: parameters are facts; paper text not redistributed

families: perception: nearest-neighbour sphere spacing, (111) layer spacing
inference: reflected wavelength from geometry + refractive index (Bragg–Snell)
design selection: choose the sphere diameter that gives a target colour
cells.risks: Effective refractive index is a model input and must be stated in the question.

sources.what: Two graphene layers (a = 2.46 Å) twisted by ~1.1° (magic angle; Cao et al., Nature 556, 43 (2018)); STM moiré periods 12.3-12.7 nm at 1.13°
sources.download: none (structure built from lattice constant and twist angle)

families: perception: moiré period / twist angle from an atomic patch (~10^4 atoms)
inference: link between twist angle and the flat-band (magic-angle) condition, with paper evidence
cells.risks: Rigid-twist model: real small-angle bilayers relax; the question must state the rigid model.

sources.what: Mesoscopic metal rings of 0.1-1 µm; oscillation period ΔB = h/(eA) from the enclosed area (e.g. Webb et al., PRL 54, 2696 (1985))

families: inference: AB period from ring geometry (area from a supplied outline)
cells.risks: Geometry is thin (an outline, not an atomic structure); twisted bilayers at ~0.1° (≥100 nm moiré) need millions of atoms. Needs a decision from the professor.

sources.what: Empirical size–band-gap sizing curves (e.g. Yu et al., Chem. Mater. 15, 2854 (2003))

families: inference: band gap from particle size measured on a supplied nanocrystal model
cells.risks: Empirical curve with stated validity range.

sources.what: Host structures already in docs/assets (β-CD, DM-β-CD, WP6) with experimentally measured guest binding free energies from the SAMPL9 challenge
sources.download: binding data table only (small text file)

families: inference: which guest binds more strongly (measured ΔG)
design selection: choose the guest meeting a binding target — experimental evidence, not computed
cells.risks: Binding depends on more than geometry; questions must state that the measured ΔG is the criterion.

sources.what: 1CRN, 1UBQ, 6LYZ, 1EHZ already in docs/assets; HELIX/SHEET records as secondary-structure evidence

families: inference: secondary-structure region from φ/ψ with the entry's own HELIX/SHEET record as evidence
cells.risks: HELIX/SHEET records are author assignments; state that they are the criterion.
